keyVerseText: And lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
rootMeaning: The Greek adjective ἀγαπητός (agapētós) derives from the verb ἀγαπάω (agapáō), which means to love in a social or moral sense. This root emphasizes a love that is deliberate and chosen rather than merely emotional, highlighting a beloved status grounded in committed affection. Therefore, ἀγαπητός carries the sense of being dearly or well loved, reflecting a relationship marked by valued and intentional love beyond a casual fondness.
usageInScripture: With 62 occurrences, ἀγαπητός consistently appears as a term expressing deep affection and value, most commonly translated as 'beloved' (31 times) and 'Beloved' (10 times). Other renderings such as 'dearly beloved,' 'dear,' and 'wellbeloved' reinforce its strong connotation of cherished relationship. This range of translations shows the word’s use both as a personal term of endearment and as a formal address among believers, underscoring its role in expressing intimate and chosen love within the biblical text.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, ἀγαπητός reveals the nature of divine and interpersonal love as intentional and treasured. It is applied by God to Christ and by Christians to one another, illustrating that believers are not only loved but are beloved in a way that denotes a special, honored status. This word enriches our understanding of Christian identity as those who are deeply and personally loved by God, which calls for a reciprocal love among believers. Recognizing this belovedness invites believers to rest in God’s pleasure and to live out love that reflects the character of God’s own agapē love.
keyVerseReflection: In Matthew 3:17, the voice from heaven declares Jesus as 'my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.' The use of ἀγαπητός here emphasizes that Jesus is uniquely and deeply loved by the Father, highlighting the intimate and approving relationship within the Trinity. This belovedness affirms Jesus’ divine identity and mission, reassuring believers of the perfect love and pleasure God has in His Son, which is foundational for Christian faith and assurance.
